issues.t: Air suspension compressor failure
issues.sym: A suspension fault or 'Normal height only' message, the SUV won't raise to off-road height, it takes a long time to reach ride height, or the compressor runs loudly and often.
issues.why: The electric air compressor that pumps up the air springs wears out, overheats from working too hard, or lets in moisture. Blocked filters, bad wiring and small air leaks make it run longer and fail sooner.
issues.next: Have the suspension codes read before replacing parts; Land Rover warned that some compressors were replaced when the real fault was elsewhere. Fix any air leak at the same time or the new compressor will wear out too.

issues.t: Air springs leak and the SUV sags
issues.sym: One corner or the whole vehicle sits low after being parked, the tires get close to the wheel arches, the ride turns bouncy, or the body leans unevenly.
issues.why: The rubber air springs (air struts) crack with age and leak, and the plastic air lines and fittings can leak too. Worn ride-height sensors can also confuse the system.
issues.next: Don't drive far if the SUV is sitting on its bump stops, because tires can rub and handling suffers. Have a shop leak-test the springs, lines and valve block and check the height sensors.

issues.t: Timing chain rattle on cold start
issues.sym: A rattle from the front of the engine for a few seconds after a cold start that gets longer and louder over time, sometimes with a check engine light and cam timing codes (P0016-P0019).
issues.why: On the 5.0L V8, the plastic chain guides turn brittle and the hydraulic tensioners lose pressure, letting the chains slap. It is an interference engine, so a failed chain can wreck it. Land Rover improved the parts for later engines.
issues.next: Have it checked as soon as you hear it. Replacing the chains, guides and tensioners early costs far less than a new engine. Keep oil changes short (about once a year or 5,000 miles).

issues.t: Coolant leak from plastic crossover pipes
issues.sym: Low coolant warnings, a sweet smell after driving, coolant on the top or back of the engine, or the temperature gauge rising.
issues.why: Plastic coolant pipes in the valley of the 5.0L V8, under the intake or supercharger, turn brittle with heat and crack.
issues.next: Don't keep topping up and driving; overheating can damage the heads. The intake or supercharger has to come off to reach the pipes, so replace the water pump and thermostat housing at the same time if they are old.

issues.t: Water pump or thermostat housing leak
issues.sym: Coolant drips under the front of the engine, crusty residue near the pump or thermostat, low coolant warnings, or the engine running hot.
issues.why: Water pumps and plastic thermostat housings on these V6 and V8 engines often start leaking somewhere between about 50,000 and 90,000 miles. Land Rover has issued several bulletins for low coolant warnings and coolant leaks on later models.
issues.next: Have the cooling system pressure-tested to find the leak. Fix it before it overheats the engine.

issues.t: Supercharger coupler rattle at idle
issues.sym: A metal rattle or knock from the front of the engine at idle that goes away with a bit of throttle. It is often mistaken for timing chain noise. A louder supercharger whine can mean the bearings are going.
issues.why: A rubber isolator (coupler) in the supercharger's front snout wears out with heat and age, so the drive gears rattle.
issues.next: Have a mechanic confirm where the noise is coming from. A coupler is a fairly modest job if caught before the snout bearings are damaged.

issues.t: Supercharger coolant pump failure
issues.sym: Reduced power, a check engine light, or a coolant warning on the supercharged 4.2L.
issues.why: The small electric pump that circulates coolant through the supercharger's intercooler fails, so the intake air runs hot.
issues.next: Have the codes read and the pump checked. It is a fairly simple swap.

issues.t: Worn front control arm bushings and ball joints
issues.sym: Clunks over bumps, a wandering or vague feel, steering wheel shake, or uneven tire wear.
issues.why: This heavy SUV wears out the rubber bushings and ball joints in the front lower control arms.
issues.next: Have the front end inspected. Arms are usually replaced as complete units, followed by an alignment.

issues.t: Parking brake screeches or won't release
issues.sym: A screeching or grinding noise from the rear when the electronic parking brake works, a parking brake warning, or the brake not releasing.
issues.why: The electronic parking brake uses a motor-driven actuator that pulls cables to the rear brakes. The actuator and cables wear or seize.
issues.next: Have the parking brake system scanned and the rear shoes and cables checked. Don't force the car to move against a stuck brake.

issues.t: Rear brakes wear out quickly
issues.sym: Squealing or grinding from the rear brakes, a brake pad warning, or vibration when stopping.
issues.why: Owners report rear pads and rotors wearing faster than expected on this heavy SUV, and rear brake lines can rust in salty areas.
issues.next: Check the rear brakes at every service. Replace pads and rotors together and inspect the brake lines for rust.

issues.t: Battery drain and no-start
issues.sym: The SUV won't start after sitting, low battery warnings, or electronics acting strangely.
issues.why: These SUVs draw a lot of power from the 12-volt battery. A failing key fob transponder has drained one owner's battery, and Land Rover has issued bulletins for low battery warnings and no-starts on later models.
issues.next: Have the battery and charging system tested and a parasitic draw test done. Use a battery maintainer if the SUV sits for long periods.

issues.t: Diesel crankshaft or bearing failure
issues.sym: Knocking from the engine that gets louder under load, sometimes with a low oil pressure warning.
issues.why: The 3.0L V6 diesel is known for costly crankshaft and bearing failures, and short trips can thin the oil with fuel.
issues.next: Stop driving if the engine knocks or the oil light comes on. Have the oil level and pressure checked and the engine inspected.

issues.t: Plug-in hybrid charging and electrical faults
issues.sym: The P400e won't charge, charging stops early, or hybrid system warnings appear.
issues.why: Reviewers and owners report charging problems and electrical faults on the plug-in hybrid.
issues.next: Try another charger and cable first, then have the dealer check for software updates and hybrid system codes. Buy one only with a solid warranty.

issues.t: Infotainment freezes or crashes
issues.sym: The touchscreen freezes, reboots or goes black, often when using Apple CarPlay.
issues.why: Software faults in the InControl infotainment system.
issues.next: Ask the dealer to load the latest infotainment software. A system reset can help in the meantime.

issues.t: Door won't lock or latch
issues.sym: One door doesn't lock with the others, the handle won't latch, or the car warns a door is open.
issues.why: Central locking motors in the door latches fail.
issues.next: Lock the SUV and check each door. A failing latch needs replacement; also check for the door latch recalls on 2014-2016 models.

issues.t: Oil or transmission cooler line leak
issues.sym: Oil or reddish fluid spots under the SUV, a burning smell, or a transmission warning.
issues.why: Steel cooler lines rust in salty climates and can burst, and Land Rover has issued bulletins for transmission fluid and cooler pipe leaks.
issues.next: Have the lines inspected at each service, especially in snow states. A burst line can strand you and starve the transmission or engine of oil.

issues.t: Mild-hybrid drive belt shreds
issues.sym: A squeal or slapping noise from the engine, then a battery or charging warning and possibly overheating.
issues.why: Land Rover issued bulletins for the main drive belt shredding on mild-hybrid 6-cylinder models.
issues.next: Stop and have it towed if a charging or temperature warning comes on after a belt noise; the belt drives the starter-generator and cooling parts.

issues.t: Front suspension knuckle can crack (recall)
issues.sym: Clunking from the front suspension or the SUV pulling, though often there is no warning.
issues.why: The upper ball joint area of the front knuckle can crack, letting a suspension arm separate and causing loss of control.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. Dealers add a retaining bracket or replace the knuckle for free.

issues.t: Doors can look shut but be unlatched (recall)
issues.sym: A door seems closed but is not fully latched and could open while driving.
issues.why: A fault in the keyless 'soft close' latches can leave a door unlatched. Earlier repairs were not always enough, so several follow-up recalls were issued.
issues.next: Check your VIN for every door latch recall, even if one was done before. Push on each door after closing it until the fix is done.

issues.t: Fuel tank outlet flange can crack and leak (recall)
issues.sym: Fuel smell around the SUV or wet spots under the fuel tank.
issues.why: The fuel outlet flange on top of the tank can crack, letting fuel leak and raising fire risk.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and have the free flange replacement done. Don't park in a garage if you smell fuel.

issues.t: Transmission may not lock in Park (recall)
issues.sym: The shifter shows Park but the SUV can still roll.
issues.why: A faulty parking pawl guide plate may keep Park from engaging, risking a rollaway. A separate early recall fixed keys that could be removed outside Park.
issues.next: Always set the parking brake. Check your VIN to confirm both 2006 recalls were completed.

issues.t: Driver airbag wiring in steering wheel can break (recall)
issues.sym: Airbag warning light on.
issues.why: Wiring in the steering wheel clockspring can fracture, so the driver airbag might not deploy fully.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and have the free repair done.

issues.t: Brake vacuum hose can wear through (recall)
issues.sym: A hard brake pedal or longer stopping distances, sometimes with a hissing sound.
issues.why: A misrouted vacuum hose can rub through, causing a loss of power brake assist.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls; dealers reroute and, if needed, replace the hose for free.

issues.t: Loose connecting rod bolts can seize the engine (recall)
issues.sym: Knocking from the engine, loss of power or a sudden engine failure.
issues.why: Some engines were built with connecting rod bolts that were not tightened correctly.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. Affected engines were replaced free.

issues.t: Rear camera image can blank out from water (recall)
issues.sym: The rearview camera shows a blank, fuzzy or distorted image.
issues.why: Water can get into the rear camera. An earlier fix was replaced by a newer one.
issues.next: Check your VIN; dealers add a seal or replace and calibrate the camera free.

issues.t: Blocked cam carrier oil channel can cause oil leak and fire (recall)
issues.sym: Oil seeping from the top of the engine or a burning oil smell, though often no sign.
issues.why: An oil channel in the engine's cam carrier can block and push oil out of a seal onto hot parts.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. Dealers inspect and replace parts as needed for free.

issues.t: DC/DC converter overload can cut power and lights (recall)
issues.sym: Loss of drive power, battery warnings, or exterior lights going out while driving.
issues.why: On mild-hybrid and plug-in models, the converter that charges the 12-volt system can overload during heavy electrical demand and shut down. A software error makes it worse.
issues.next: Check your VIN for both converter recalls and have the free software update done. If warnings appear, pull over safely.

issues.t: Oil filter housing can crack and leak (recall)
issues.sym: Oil leak at the front of the engine, low oil warning or a burning smell.
issues.why: The oil filter housing can crack and leak oil onto hot parts, raising fire risk.
issues.next: Check your VIN; dealers replace the housing, filter and seals for free.

issues.t: Transmission can shift to neutral and lose power (recall)
issues.sym: The SUV suddenly loses drive as if in neutral, with transmission warnings.
issues.why: Transmission oil pressure can drop, letting the clutches release.
issues.next: Check your VIN; dealers inspect and replace the transmission as needed.

issues.t: Rear subframe can crack (recall)
issues.sym: Knocking from the rear or a change in handling, though cracks may not be noticeable.
issues.why: Cracks can form in the rear subframe that holds the rear suspension.
issues.next: Check your VIN. Dealers inspect and replace the subframe once the final fix is available.

issues.t: Panoramic sunroof side trim can come off (recall)
issues.sym: Wind noise or a loose trim strip along the sunroof edge.
issues.why: The side finisher trim may not have been secured and can fly off.
issues.next: Check your VIN; dealers inspect and secure the trim for free.

issues.t: Moisture can make tail lights fail (recall)
issues.sym: Fog in the right tail light or tailgate light, or lights not working.
issues.why: Moisture can get into the right-side tailgate and body lamps. A separate recall covers taillights that may not show brake lights correctly.
issues.next: Check your VIN for both lighting recalls; dealers replace the lamps free.

issues.t: Gear position display may not light (recall)
issues.sym: The gear indicator on the shifter doesn't show which gear is selected.
issues.why: Moisture got into the gear shift module during assembly.
issues.next: Check the gear on the instrument display before moving. Dealers replace the shift module free.

issues.t: Rear middle seat belt may not latch (recall)
issues.sym: The second-row center belt clicks in but doesn't stay latched.
issues.why: A manufacturing error in the buckle.
issues.next: Don't seat anyone in the middle until the buckle is replaced free.

issues.t: Seat belt reminder chime may not sound (recall)
issues.sym: No chime when a front belt is unbuckled.
issues.why: A faulty audio amplifier.
issues.next: Check your VIN; the amplifier is replaced free.
